name: Bean Common Mosaic Virus
description: A seed-borne viral disease causing mosaic patterns, leaf distortion, and stunting in common beans. It is transmitted by aphids and through infected seeds, reducing yield and seed quality.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves
Leaf distortion, blistering, and downward curling
Stunted plant growth with shortened internodes
Seeds from infected plants may show discoloration
causes: Bean common mosaic virus (BCMV), a potyvirus
Seed-borne virus in infected seeds (primary source)
Transmitted by aphid vectors (Myzus persicae, Aphis fabae)
treatments: No curative treatment for viral infection
Control aphid vectors with neem oil or insecticidal soap
Use reflective mulches to repel aphids
prevention: Rogue infected plants as soon as symptoms appear
Control weeds that serve as virus reservoirs
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
